questions.text: In this lesson, tasks/get returns resultType="complete" with status="working". What does that mean?

options.A: The polling RPC finished, while the represented job is still running.
options.B: The job finished, but its final result has not been downloaded.
options.C: The response is invalid because complete requires status completed.
options.D: The task has become a persistent protocol session.

questions.explanation: The outer resultType describes completion of the tasks/get RPC; status describes the durable job’s separate lifecycle.

questions.text: An already-created task pauses with status="input_required" and an approve_outline input request. How does the client submit the answer in this lesson’s task flow?

options.A: Retry the original tools/call without its taskId.
options.B: Send a server-initiated elicitation request back to the worker.
options.C: Call tasks/result with the approval embedded in headers.
options.D: Call tasks/update with the taskId and keyed inputResponses.

questions.explanation: Input after task creation is submitted through tasks/update for that durable task. Retrying the original tool call is the pre-task core MRTR pattern.

questions.text: A task has status="completed". The supplied tasks_cancel method changes status only when it is outside TERMINAL_STATUSES={"completed","cancelled","failed"}. What happens when it is called for this task with valid ownership and capabilities?

options.A: It changes the status to cancelled and deletes the completed result.
options.B: It preserves completed and returns an empty complete acknowledgement.
options.C: It raises -32602 because completed tasks cannot be looked up.
options.D: It restarts the worker so cancellation can be applied.

questions.explanation: Completed is terminal, so the mutation block is skipped and tasks_cancel returns complete() without changing the result.
